rmk:
A quite long recording of a displaying Common snipe. It isn't always easy to get it right because some birds draw pretty large circles. I'd chose to stand at its very edge so that I could get some decent quality when it was flying overhead. That also means that only 10% of its display is recorded clear, while the rest of the recording sounds more faint. I didn't want to cut out the long faint parts because then it wouldn't give the realistic image of these birds display flights as it is shown now.
At 1:42, you can hear the birds wingbeats as it is tumbling down towards me and my microphone because of an unkown reason. He might have had spotted a raptor? I don't know. Immediately after, he started to climb up again and continued his way. There is a river at a distance that cause some backgroundnoise. No filters used, original recording.

rmk: Common Snipe calling in the vicinity of a perched male Cuckoo. The Common Snipe sounds consist mainly of 'whickering' rather than drumming. Actual drumming is not that loud but occurs for around two seconds after the eighth, eleventh and twentieth seconds. The Cuckoo was calling from the same perch for around three hours. As well as its main call, it also uttered short, staccato calls that could be likened to a cough or a sneeze. To my ears, the call is somewhat reminiscent of certain gamebird vocalisations, especially grouse. Occasionally, the call is repeated in a short series (0:56), suggestive of a Willow Grouse bursting into flight. Single utterances can be heard  at 0:15, 0:21, 0:25, 0:28 and, after 'cuc-koo' calls, calling, at 0:50, 0:53. I was not present to observe the scene - but it sounds as though the Cuckoo may have uttered its staccato notes in response to the presence of the Common Snipe - because it was piqued by the proximity of the Common Snipe's overhead drumming?
